# Design system: tokens, themes, breakpoints, fonts, contrast

Design tokens and the themes that read them, breakpoints, the site's guidelines, fonts (the upload doors and the ops they write) and the contrast records only a person makes.

[`token.set`](#tokenset) · [`font.add`](#fontadd) · [`font.remove`](#fontremove) · [`theme.set`](#themeset) · [`themeSet.set`](#themesetset) · [`guideline.set`](#guidelineset) · [`breakpoint.set`](#breakpointset) · [`breakpoint.rename`](#breakpointrename) · [`contrast.correct`](#contrastcorrect) · [`contrast.correctLayout`](#contrastcorrectlayout) · [`contrast.bypass`](#contrastbypass) · [`contrast.unbypass`](#contrastunbypass) · [`contrast.restoreBypass`](#contrastrestorebypass) · [`contrast.dropBypass`](#contrastdropbypass) · [`font.uploadFace`](#fontuploadface) · [`font.addGoogle`](#fontaddgoogle) · [`font.setFace`](#fontsetface)

## token.set

Set or clear one design token in one of the site's token sets: a colour, a size, a font, a shadow, an easing, an alias of another token, or a group's extension. Every style that reads the token follows. Breakpoints are breakpoint.set's, a font file font.add's, a theme's own set themeSet.set's. Refusals: `invalid_input` (a path segment outside a-z, 0-9 and `-`), `token.extension_unknown` (an `$extensions.libretto` key Libretto does not know); the validator's `ref.token` (an alias to no token). A colour change that leaves a text failing AA is corrected in the same step by the contrast check, or refused.

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "colour", "color", "palette", "brand", "font", "typography", "spacing".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set` | string | yes | The token set, one the `tokens` read names (`core`, `semantic-light` on a converted site). |
| `path` | string (max 200) | yes | Dot path of the token or group (`color.palette.brand.500`); a segment may be `$description` or `$extensions`. |
| `token` | string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>> \| null | yes | The DTCG token or group written there: `{ $type: 'color', $value: '#1e3d4f' }`, an alias `{ $type: 'color', $value: '{color.palette.ink.700}' }`; null clears it. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"set":"core","path":"color.palette.brand.500","token":{"$type":"color","$value":"#2f6f8f","$description":"Accento del marchio"}}
```
```json
{"set":"semantic-light","path":"color.text.accent","token":{"$type":"color","$value":"{color.palette.brand.600}"}}
```

## font.add

Add a web font file to the site's fonts and its face to the family's faces token, so every page that draws the family loads it. It records a file whose bytes are already stored and uploads nothing: the upload route sends it. A style draws the family through a fontFamily token (token.set) or a font-family declaration. Refused: `font.exists` (the id is taken, or the site has that face: same family, weight, style and unicode range), `font.mime` (not WOFF2, WOFF, OpenType or TrueType, or a blob of another type), `font.token` (token names something that is not a fontFamily token).

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | A new uuid you choose for the font file. |
| `font` | { name: string (min 1, max 100), familyKey?: string (max 100), fileName: string (min 1, max 255), mimeType: string (min 1, max 50), fileSize?: integer ≥0, storageKey?: string (max 500), url: string (min 1, max 2048), weight?: integer ≥1 ≤1000, style?: "normal" \| "italic", display?: "swap" \| "block" \| "fallback" \| "opti… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) | yes | The stored file: name (the family, as styles name it), fileName, mimeType (font/woff2, font/woff, font/otf, font/ttf) and url where it is stored; its weight (400 unless said), style (normal or italic), display, unicodeRange; a variable font says isVariableFont 1 and axesJson { "wght": [100, 900] }. |
| `token` | object |  | The fontFamily token the face goes on; absent: font.faces.<familyKey> of the fonts token set, made when missing. |
| `token` › `set` | string (max 100) | yes | The token set, by key. |
| `token` › `path` | string (max 300) | yes | The fontFamily token's dot path in the set (font.family.heading). |
| `index` | integer ≥0 |  | Its place among that token's faces; absent: last. |
| `face` | false |  | false: the file only, with no face (what the undo of removing a font that had none writes). |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"4c8e2a6f-1d3b-4f97-8a5c-6e0b2d9f3a71","font":{"name":"Sul Sans","familyKey":"sul-sans","fileName":"SulSans-Bold.woff2","mimeType":"font/woff2","fileSize":27410,"url":"/api/fonts/archiplan/SulSans-Bold.woff2","storageKey":"archiplan/fonts/SulSans-Bold.woff2","weight":700,"style":"normal","display":"swap","source":"upload"}}
```

## font.remove

Take a font file out of the site's fonts, with its face; the faces token goes with its last face. Refused: `font.unknown`, `font.inUse` (the family's last face while a token or a style names the family, naming them; send evenIfUsed to remove it anyway), `font.faceSet` (its face is in another token set: name it in set), `font_legacy` (a font with fields its undo could not add back).

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "font".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | yes | The font file, by id (the design read lists the site's fonts). |
| `evenIfUsed` | true |  | true: remove the family's last face although tokens or styles still name the family (they fall back to the next font of their stack). |
| `set` | string (max 100) |  | The token set holding its face, when not the fonts set. |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"4c8e2a6f-1d3b-4f97-8a5c-6e0b2d9f3a71"}
```

## theme.set

Set or remove one theme of the site, whole: its label, the token sets it reads in order, whether it is a draft and where it applies by itself. A draft is offered to no page or section until published; `activation` applies it by colour scheme, host or address prefix. To change one field, send the theme as it stands with that field changed. Which theme is the default does not change by edit. Refused with `theme.default` (making another theme the default, clearing the default, or a draft or activation on the default) and `theme.known` (a token set the site lacks, which themeSet.set adds; or removing a theme a part or a style names).

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "colour", "color", "dark".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string (max 100) | yes | The theme's key (`light`, `dark`), as the site read lists the themes; a new key adds a theme. |
| `theme` | { label: string (min 1, max 80), sets: string (max 100)[] (≤16), isDefault?: true, draft?: true, activation?: { prefersColorScheme?: "light" \| "dark", hostname?: string (max 253), pathPrefix?: string (max 200) } } \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<strin… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) | yes | The theme whole: `label`, `sets` (token set keys in order, a later one wins), `draft: true` to keep it off pages until published, `activation` ({ prefersColorScheme: light or dark, hostname, pathPrefix }: where it applies by itself), `isDefault` as it stands. Null removes it. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"key":"dark","theme":{"label":"Scuro","sets":["core","semantic-light","semantic-dark"],"activation":{"prefersColorScheme":"dark"}}}
```
```json
{"key":"sera","theme":{"label":"Sera","sets":["core","semantic-light","semantic-sera"],"draft":true}}
```

## themeSet.set

Set or remove one token set a non-default theme reads, a DTCG token tree whose tokens win over the sets before it in the theme. The tree replaces the stored set. The default tokens are token.set's. Refused with `theme.known` (the key is a set of the default tokens, or a theme still reads the set being removed).

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "dark".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string (max 100) | yes | The token set's key (`semantic-dark`): one a theme lists in its `sets`, never a set of the default tokens. |
| `tokens` | Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>>> \| null | yes | The set whole, a DTCG token tree (groups of tokens with `$value` and `$type`); null removes it. |

Example input:

```json
{"key":"semantic-dark","tokens":{"color":{"surface":{"$type":"color","$value":"#151514"},"text":{"$type":"color","$value":"#f4f1ea"}}}}
```

## guideline.set

Set or clear one guideline rule: for a role, an op or op prefix and optionally a style property, whether it is fixed, free or a choice of tokens, with the note people read. A fixed rule refuses that role's batches with `guideline.fixed`; a choice rule refuses a style value outside its token group with `guideline.choice`. Where several rules match, the most specific wins (design system, then property, then op, then role), and fixed over choice over free. Discovery shows each op's verdict for the caller. A rule of null removes it. Refused: `invalid_input` (the stored guidelines are not rules).

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The rule's id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes; setting an id again replaces its rule. |
| `rule` | { role: string (min 1, max 40), op: string, property?: string (min 1, max 80), designSystem?: true, mode: "fixed" \| "free" \| { choice: { tokens: string (max 100) } }, note: string (min 1, max 300) } \| null | yes | The rule, or null to remove it. role: a role (designer, editor) or "*"; op: an op name, a prefix ending in ".*" or "*"; property: the style property it governs; designSystem: true for ops that write the design system only; mode: "fixed", "free" or { choice: { tokens: <token group> } }; note: what the person reads. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"id":"colori-testo","rule":{"role":"editor","op":"tree.set_style","property":"color","mode":{"choice":{"tokens":"color.text"}},"note":"I colori del testo vengono dalla palette dello studio."}}
```
```json
{"id":"motion-fixed","rule":{"role":"editor","op":"timeline.*","mode":"fixed","note":"Le animazioni le cura il designer."}}
```
```json
{"id":"motion-fixed","rule":null}
```

## breakpoint.set

Set or clear one breakpoint: the media query a `bp:<name>` style scope stands for. To rename one, use breakpoint.rename, which rewrites every style that names it. Refused with `breakpoint.shadowed` (another token set holds it: edit it there), `breakpoint.unknown` (clearing one the set lacks) and `scope.known` (clearing a breakpoint a style still names).

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "mobile", "phone", "responsive".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The breakpoint's name: what a `bp:<name>` style scope names (`md`, `wide-desktop`). |
| `query` | string (min 1, max 300) \| null | yes | The media query it stands for: `(min-width: 768px)`, `print`, `screen and (min-width: 1024px)`; null clears the breakpoint. |
| `set` | string (max 100) |  | The token set that holds it; absent: `breakpoints`, where the site keeps them. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"name":"md","query":"(min-width: 768px)"}
```
```json
{"name":"chart","query":null}
```

## breakpoint.rename

Give a breakpoint another name, in one step: every style scope, component cell, motion, picture source and token value that names it names the new one. Refused with `breakpoint.taken` (the new name is `base` or another breakpoint's), `breakpoint.shadowed` (another token set holds it: rename it there), `breakpoint.fixed` (a document viewer spreads from it by name) and `breakpoint.unknown`.

- **op**; class `design` (Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes | The breakpoint's name now. |
| `to` | string | yes | Its new name: lower-case words joined by `-`, not `base` and no other breakpoint's. |
| `set` | string (max 100) |  | The token set that holds it; absent: `breakpoints`, where the site keeps them. |

Example input:

```json
{"from":"chart","to":"tablet"}
```

## contrast.correct

Set a text's colour in one scope to a colour that passes AA on its ground: the correction the contrast check writes itself when a batch settles, with the pair, both colours and both ratios. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved. An undo runs it back. To fix a pair yourself, set the text's colour with tree.set_style or instance.override; contrast/<pageId> lists the pairs. Refused: `contrast.uncorrectable` (the text is not a page node or an inner node of an instance on the page).

- **op**; class `reserved` (no one sends it: Libretto writes it); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| `text` | string | yes |  |
| `ground` | string \| "canvas" | yes |  |
| `scope` | string (max 300) | yes | When a style holds: `base` (always), or parts joined by `\|`, all of which hold (`bp:md\|s:hover`). Each part is `<prefix>:<value>`: `bp:<name>` from a breakpoint of the site up (mobile first; names such as sm, md, lg, xl are in the tokens read); `mq:<media query>` (`mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `mq:(hover: none)`); `cq:<container query>`; `s:<state>` the node's own state (`s:hover`, `s:focus-visible`, `s:active`, `s:current`, `s:open`, `s:checked`, `s:empty`, `s:loaded`, `s:playing`), a state the page sets on nodes (`s:scene-active`, `s:step=2`), or selector terms (`s:::after`, `s::not([href])`, `s:[aria-expanded="true"]`); `a:<state>` the same state held by an ancestor (`a:hover`: the link or button around it is hovered); `pg:<state>=<value>` a page state, any of several values (`pg:menu=open`, `pg:menu=closed,open`); `p:<part>` a named part of the widget it is (`p:track`); `sub:<subset>` the items of a repeat subset; `st:enter` the style it starts from when it first shows; `sp:word` or `sp:char` each word or letter of a split text; `t:<selector>` its descendants (`t: a`, `t:> li`); `th:<theme>` where that theme applies; `fmt:<format>` when drawn in that output format. |
| `property` | "color" \| "fill" \| "stroke" | yes |  |
| `color` | string (max 4000) \| number \| { $token: string } \| { $cell: string } \| { $prop: string } \| { $item: string } \| { $state: string } \| { $bind: string (max 80), template?: string (min 1, max 80), fallback?: string (max 200), pair?: { foreground: string (min 3, max 120), background: string (min 3, max 120), theme?: string (… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) | yes | A value: CSS text or a number (`"1.5rem"`, `600`), a token (`{ "$token": "color.text" }`), a cell of the component (`{ "$cell": "<variant>.<size>.<state>.<part>.<bp>.<property>" }`), a prop of the component it is inside (`{ "$prop": "title" }`), a field of the repeat item around it (`{ "$item": "title" }`), a page state (`{ "$state": "menu" }`), a value the page reads when it renders (`{ "$bind": "item.title" }`), a choice on a prop or state (`{ "$switch": { "on": { "$prop": "tone" }, "cases": { "dark": "#111" } } }`) or a formatted value (`$format`). |

## contrast.bypass

Keep a text and ground pair as it is although it fails AA or cannot be measured: a record on the page of who, when, the ratio it measures and why. It is a person's decision, the site administrator's: an agent cannot send it, and asks a person to accept the pair in Libretto, or fixes the colour instead. Text "*" keeps every text on a ground that cannot be measured (a moving, blended or pictured ground), through later text edits. A second bypass of a pair replaces its record. Refused: `contrast.unknown_pair` (the page has no such pair, or the ground makes no text unmeasurable), `contrast.unmeasured`, `unknown_page`.

- **op**; class `contrast` (a person: Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | uuid | yes | The page the pair is on (site_context lists the pages; contrast/<pageId> reads its pairs). |
| `text` | string \| "*" | yes | The text's id as contrast/<pageId> names it (an instance's inner text: <instance>-<node>); "*": every text on the ground. |
| `ground` | string \| "canvas" | yes | The ground's id as contrast/<pageId> names it, or canvas: the page itself. |
| `reason` | string (min 1, max 500) | yes | Why the pair stays as it is, in the words people read in History and on the page's checks. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"pageId":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2","text":"5zfqbql3","ground":"x576co7y","reason":"Il grigio chiaro è quello del marchio: lo studio lo tiene anche se il contrasto è basso."}
```
```json
{"pageId":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2","text":"*","ground":"38c3kvuc","reason":"Le foto in dissolvenza cambiano sotto il titolo: lo controlla lo studio a ogni nuova foto."}
```

## contrast.unbypass

Take the bypass off a pair: the next write that touches the page judges the pair again and corrects it if it fails. Like contrast.bypass, it is the site administrator's alone; an agent cannot send it. Refused: `op_target` (the pair has no bypass).

- **op**; class `contrast` (a person: Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

| `ground` | string \| "canvas" | yes | The ground's id as contrast/<pageId> names it, or canvas: the page itself. |


## contrast.dropBypass

Take the bypass record off a pair whose node left the page: the contrast check writes it in the batch that removes the node. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved. Undoing that batch puts the record back (contrast.restoreBypass). Refused: `op_target` (the pair has no bypass).

- **op**; class `reserved` (no one sends it: Libretto writes it); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.

|---|---|---|---|
| `pageId` | uuid | yes | The page the pair is on (site_context lists the pages; contrast/<pageId> reads its pairs). |
| `text` | string \| "*" | yes | The text's id as contrast/<pageId> names it (an instance's inner text: <instance>-<node>); "*": every text on the ground. |
| `ground` | string \| "canvas" | yes | The ground's id as contrast/<pageId> names it, or canvas: the page itself. |

Example input:

```json
{"pageId":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2","text":"5zfqbql3","ground":"x576co7y"}
```

## font.uploadFace

Add one face of a font family from a WOFF2, WOFF, TTF or OTF file (stored as WOFF2), with its weight (or a variable file's range), style, display, fallback and licence note. A face the library already holds is refused. Alone in a batch. The file travels as base64 in `data`, at most 20 MB per call; an archive or a larger file is refused with where a person uploads it. Every check of the admin's upload holds (type, size, content, the site's quota). A dry run makes the checks with nothing stored. Answers the write with `id`, the face's font id.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `design` (Administrator); no confirmation; dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back; limit: 60 uploads a minute per token, dry runs included.
- Found by the plain words: "upload", "font".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `fileName` | string (min 1, max 255) | yes |
| `contentType` | string (min 1, max 127) |  |
| `data` | string (min 1) | yes |
| `name` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes |
| `weight` | integer ≥1 ≤1000 \| [integer ≥1 ≤1000, integer ≥1 ≤1000] |  |
| `style` | "normal" \| "italic" |  |
| `display` | "swap" \| "block" \| "fallback" \| "optional" |  |
| `fallbackStack` | string (max 255) \| null |  |
| `licence` | string (max 2000) \| null |  |
| `variation` | Record<string, number> \| null |  |
| `load` | "auto" \| "critical" \| "deferred" |  |
| `fallback` | "arial" \| "times" \| "georgia" \| "courier" \| "menlo" \| "none" |  |

Example input:

```json
{"fileName":"Inter-Bold.woff2","data":"<base64>","name":"Inter","weight":700}
```

## font.addGoogle

Self-host a Google Fonts family in the weights asked, upright and (`italic`) italic: every face is fetched from Google, checked and stored, and lands as one step or not at all. Alone in a batch; a dry run fetches and checks with nothing stored.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `design` (Administrator); no confirmation; dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back; limit: 60 uploads a minute per token, dry runs included.
- Found by the plain words: "upload", "font", "typography".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes |
| `weights` | integer ≥100 ≤900[] (≤9) | yes |
| `italic` | boolean |  |
| `display` | "swap" \| "block" \| "fallback" \| "optional" |  |
| `load` | "auto" \| "critical" \| "deferred" |  |
| `fallback` | "arial" \| "times" \| "georgia" \| "courier" \| "menlo" \| "none" |  |

Example input:

```json
{"family":"Inter","weights":[400,700],"italic":false}
```

## font.setFace

Change a face's settings, as Design's face settings do: how it loads, the axes it pins (checked against its file), its fallback face (measured from the file). Alone in a batch; one undo restores it.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `design` (Administrator); no confirmation; dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back; limit: 60 uploads a minute per token, dry runs included.
- Found by the plain words: "font".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes |
| `load` | "auto" \| "critical" \| "deferred" |  |
| `variation` | Record<string, number> \| null |  |
| `fallback` | { against?: "arial" \| "times" \| "georgia" \| "courier" \| "menlo", sizeAdjust?: number ≥0 ≤1000, ascentOverride?: number ≥0 ≤1000, descentOverride?: number ≥0 ≤1000, lineGapOverride?: number ≥0 ≤1000 } \| null |  |

Example input:

```json
{"id":"<fontId>","load":"swap","variation":{"opsz":72}}
```
